While Apple's overhauled personal assistant is undoubtedly the headlining feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate, this year's update includes plenty of other new features and improvements that have nothing to do with Siri AI. After reading this article, I've handpicked a few of my favorite new features in macOS 27—be sure to also check out my video where I'll demo each one for you.

App icons get a major overhaul

macOS 27 has made some sort of change to nearly every built-in app icon, with a handful—such as Siri, Preview, and Chess—getting completely redesigned from the ground up. Other app icons, like Finder, Photos, and Reminders, have received noticeable refreshes, trending toward a stronger emphasis on the Liquid Glass design language. In macOS Golden Gate, very few app icons have been spared changes, though many of the updates are quite subtle.

If you watch the video below, you'll see a slider comparison showing the differences for each app icon between macOS Tahoe and the new macOS Golden Gate.

Some of the updates, like the Photos app, I'm a big fan of. Others, like Finder, I'm not fully sold on yet. Drop your thoughts on these app icon changes in the comments below.

Video: macOS 27 top features and changes

Comprehensive HDR support

One of the coolest things about macOS 27 is its comprehensive HDR support for the operating system's visual effects. Liquid Glass design language icons, toolbars, and other elements now include support for a higher dynamic range, and users with HDR-capable displays will notice the difference immediately.

If you want to see which elements have a higher dynamic range, you can use the built-in Digital Color Meter tool in macOS to look for areas where shadows or highlights get clipped while viewing native SDR values. Be sure to check out my video where I explore different parts of the operating system to showcase the HDR support.

If you're a Studio Display XDR user, you've certainly already seen the difference, but even if you haven't purchased Apple's most expensive display, you can still enjoy these benefits on third-party HDR-capable displays.

I recently got hands-on with Asus's 32-inch 4K ProArt QD-OLED display, and thanks to its panel technology, the HDR effect across the entire operating system really stands out. Unlike Apple's first-party displays that support Extended Dynamic Range, you'll need to enable the High Dynamic Range option in Settings > Displays to enjoy these benefits.

I've also recently started using the Dell UltraSharp U3226Q QD-OLED display, and I'm really loving it—a review will be coming soon. On both displays, HDR elements really pop—one example being the cursor that flashes in the newly designed Spotlight/Siri AI interface.

Design updates

macOS Golden Gate has plenty of design updates addressing user complaints about macOS Tahoe. One of my biggest complaints was that some windows had inconsistent corner radii.

Of course, that wasn't the only complaint addressed, but it was the most important one to me. Other fixes include: floating sidebars returning to flush sidebars; improved toolbars with a visible divider line; and the Liquid Glass effect itself has been refined, including a new slider that lets users customize the ratio of transparency to tint throughout the operating system.

Streamlined menus

Another major user complaint about macOS Tahoe was how cluttered the menus became with unnecessary items. In macOS Tahoe, nearly every menu option had a corresponding symbol, making the menus look like a complete mess.

When every menu item has an icon, you eventually run out of meaningful icon options, while simultaneously making the original symbols less effective. I'm glad Apple finally fixed this issue.

iPhone Mirroring

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has three major improvements that make the feature much more useful on Golden Gate.

  • You can now access Control Center from your mirrored iPhone.
  • You can adjust the size of the iPhone Mirroring interface so that it's closer to the aspect ratio of an iPad mini.
  • You can play DRM-protected content from your iPhone on your Mac without encountering a black screen.

Without a doubt, iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has become significantly more useful!

9to5Mac's take

While Siri AI has dominated most of the news cycle, macOS Golden Gate is about more than just Siri. In this article I've highlighted some of my favorite new features, but there's still plenty more for you to discover. Watch my full video for a rundown of all the new features, and let me know in the comments below which ones are your favorites.
